extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources, and created new questions based on their expertise. They were instructed to adhere to copyright regulations and select questions without immediately available answers. Quality control involved three stages: 1) identifying and removing duplicates using lexical overlap and URL similarity, 2) format and typo checking by co-authors, and 3) categorizing problems into four difficulty levels and excluding overly simplistic ones.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students specializing in the targeted majors (including co-authors).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases introduced during the manual curation process.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited by its exclusive focus on college-level subjects, which is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI. There is no direct mapping between performance on the benchmark and the capabilities of the "90th percentile of skilled adults," and it does not cover all tasks an AGI would need to tackle.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to monitor progress towards Expert AGI, which carries significant societal implications, including the potential for job displacement and economic disruption as AI reaches the substitution threshold for human labor.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed as an evaluation benchmark for testing the multimodal understanding and reasoning capabilities of models. It is split into a few-shot development set, a validation set (for hyperparameter selection), and a test set. It is primarily used for zero-shot and few-shot evaluation rather than fine-tuning.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data cleaning process consisted of three stages: 1) identifying and removing duplicate problems using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, 2) manual checking and correction of formats and typos to ensure standardization, and 3) filtering out approximately 10% of the collected problems that were classified as 'very easy'.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI [57].

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We shall caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition [57], because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and “90th percentile of skilled adults,” nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. [...] MMMU , like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI [57].

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: It denotes an AI system that reaches “at least 90th percentile of skilled adults” in a broad range of tasks, thus starting to achieve “the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor” for many industries, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. Therefore, it is of both intellectual and societal importance to closely monitor the progress towards Expert AGI.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We introduce MMMU : a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. [...] MMMU , constituting 11.5K questions, is divided into a few-shot development set, a validation set, and a test set. [...] the validation set, useful for hyperparameter selection, contains approximately 900 questions, while the test set comprises 10.5K questions.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: To further control the quality of our data, we perform two steps of data cleaning. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. This step requires authors to ensure adherence to a standardized format, undertaking necessary corrections where deviations are found. In the third and final stage, the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels... Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.
